issues.legal_issue: Surplus land finally declared under an earlier land-tenure regime vests in the State under a later ceiling regime despite the former holder's continued possession or non-utilisation of the land.
material_facts: The land had been finally declared surplus under the earlier law.
The holders were permitted, under an exemption for cultivation as a modern farm, to remain in possession and use the surplus land.
The land remained in the holders' possession and had not been distributed when the later law came into force.
The holders relied on their continued possession and the land's non-utilisation to resist vesting.
issues.conclusion: The surplus land vested in the State under the later law; continued possession and non-utilisation did not prevent vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3) of the Haryana Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1972 unequivocally vested surplus land declared under the earlier law in the State. The court held that non-utilisation before vesting was immaterial, consistently with the statutory object of redistributing surplus land and conferring title on landless persons and agricultural labourers. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: surplus_land_vesting_dispute and prior_surplus_declaration_final and retention_authorized_by_exemption and later_law_expressly_vests_prior_surplus and continued_possession_or_nonuse_invoked_against_vesting

predicates.surplus_land_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether land previously declared surplus has vested in the State under a later land-ceiling regime.
predicates.prior_surplus_declaration_final: A competent authority had finally declared the land surplus under an earlier regime.
predicates.retention_authorized_by_exemption: The former holder remained in possession under an exemption permitting use of the surplus land.
predicates.later_law_expressly_vests_prior_surplus: A later law expressly provides for State vesting of land previously declared surplus.
predicates.continued_possession_or_nonuse_invoked_a: The former holder relies on continued possession or non-utilisation of the land to contest vesting.

issues.definition: When a vesting dispute concerns land finally declared surplus, retained under an exemption, and covered by a later law expressly vesting prior surplus, reliance on continued possession or non-use does not prevent State vesting.

issues.legal_issue: A final determination of surplus land under an earlier regime cannot be reopened and recomputed under a later regime merely because family circumstances or ceiling limits have changed.
material_facts: The surplus area had been finally determined under the earlier law.
After that determination, some family members who had been minors became majors and the family circumstances changed.
The later law reduced the applicable ceiling and provided for determination of surplus area under its own provisions.
The holders sought to reopen the earlier final determination and recompute the surplus area under the later law.
issues.conclusion: The earlier final surplus determination could not be reopened for recomputation under the later law; any additional surplus arising under the later law could be determined under that law.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7 and 9 of the Haryana Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1972 provide for determining surplus area under that Act, while Section 33(2)(ii) addresses surplus area determined in pending proceedings under the earlier law. The court found no express provision authorising reopening of a surplus determination that had already become final. It treated the legislative scheme as preserving that determination while allowing surplus arising under the later law to be determined under its provisions. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: reopening_surplus_determination_dispute and prior_surplus_determination_final and family_status_or_ceiling_changed and later_law_has_no_authority_to_reopen_final_determination

predicates.reopening_surplus_determination_dispute: The proceeding seeks to reopen a prior determination of surplus land under a later land-ceiling regime.
predicates.prior_surplus_determination_final: The earlier determination of the surplus area had become final.
predicates.family_status_or_ceiling_changed: Family circumstances or the applicable ceiling changed after the earlier determination.
predicates.later_law_has_no_authority_to_reopen_fin: The later regime contains no authority to reopen the final earlier determination.

issues.definition: If a proceeding seeks reopening of a final surplus determination after family circumstances or the ceiling have changed, and the later regime does not authorise reopening, the earlier determination remains final.

issues.legal_issue: An exemption permitting continued use of surplus land under an earlier regime does not preserve that use after a later law withdraws the exemption.
material_facts: The holders remained in possession of surplus land under an exemption permitting its use as a modern farm.
The later law expressly withdrew exemptions granted for use of surplus land under the earlier regime.
The holders continued to rely on the earlier permission to retain possession.
issues.conclusion: From the later law's appointed day, the exemption no longer authorised possession, which became unlawful and could be resumed by the competent officer.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32 of the Haryana Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1972 expressly withdrew exemptions granted under rules made under the earlier law for the utilisation of surplus area as a well-run farm, among other specified uses. The court held that possession under such an exemption became unlawful after its withdrawal and that the Collector or competent officer could resume possession. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.exemption_based_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns possession of surplus land claimed under an earlier use exemption.
predicates.possession_rested_on_earlier_use_exempti: The holder's continued possession depended on permission granted under an earlier exemption.
predicates.later_law_withdrew_that_exemption: A later law expressly withdrew the exemption on which possession depended.

issues.definition: When possession of surplus land rests on an earlier use exemption that a later law withdraws, continued possession under that exemption becomes unlawful and resumable.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal abates against a deceased appellant and the remaining appellants when legal representatives are not substituted and the cause of action is common to them.
material_facts: One appellant died while the appeal was pending.
The deceased appellant's legal representatives were not brought on record.
The cause of action underlying the appeal was common to the deceased appellant and the other appellants.
issues.conclusion: The appeal abated against the deceased appellant and, because the cause of action was common, against the other appellants as well.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the procedural consequence of a deceased appellant's legal representatives not being substituted and held that abatement extended to the other appellants where the common cause of action operated against them as well. The judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this ruling.

rule.if: civil_appeal_with_multiple_appellants and appellant_died and legal_representatives_not_substituted and cause_of_action_common_and_inseverable

predicates.civil_appeal_with_multiple_appellants: The proceeding is a civil appeal brought by more than one appellant.
predicates.appellant_died: One of the appellants died while the appeal was pending.
predicates.legal_representatives_not_substituted: The deceased appellant's legal representatives were not substituted in the appeal.
predicates.cause_of_action_common_and_inseverable: The cause of action is common to the deceased appellant and the other appellants, such that the appeal cannot proceed separately against them.

issues.definition: In a multi-appellant civil appeal, if an appellant dies without substitution of legal representatives and the cause of action is common and inseverable, the appeal abates against the deceased appellant and the remaining appellants.
